Personally, Dark Souls 3 is my least favourite.



**I think that it objectively can be seen as the best souls game though, especially for newcomers:**


- the controls and gameplay are the most polished they've ever been.


- the stat system doesn't have any trap stats (resistance or adaptability), and equip load is streamlined.


- the bosses are complex, with two phases, and a ton of moves they can use.


- the game is streamlined and more linear which gives it a decent difficulty curve.


- the presentation is fantastic and so is the art direction.


- the quality of the game and its levels is very consistent, and never gets as bad as Dks1 and 2's worse levels.




As for my issues with the game, the main one stems from its inspirations. You would expect a Dark Souls 3 to be a sequel to Dark Souls 1 and 2, and to be the best of both worlds. **But what it is instead is a sequel to Dark Souls 1 mixed with Bloodborne**.


**It takes a lot from Bloodborne:**


- the game is faster overall, and so is your character and your enemies.


- healing also is way faster, with almost the same speed as a blood vial.


- enemies rely a lot on combos, fast attacks and delayed attacks. This also makes the game rely more on your reflexes that your knowledge at some points.


- you can roll a lot even with your starting stamina. equip load barely matters as long as you're under 70%.


- poise isn't a thing anymore. it's replaced by hyperarmor that triggers when using heavy weapons certain weapon arts - if you wear heavy armor.


- armor can't be upgraded anymore and instead has an absortion system which is supposed to scale with your level.


- staggered bosses can now often be riposted for critical damage. Bosses also always have a second phase. 



While some of these changes, especially the boss battles, are great, a lot of them take away personality from the game. 


To me, Dark Souls is a game about being an unsignificant human who can't do shit at first but then grows as you fight enemies, learn new things and find new gear. In Dks3, you can start off as a knight in heavy armor, with a 100% physical reduction shield, a longsword, and can still fastroll. That says a lot about the intent of the game. 


It no longer feels the same kind of adventure, but **more focused on its action and being as epic as possible to impress the player**. It's also less grounded, with a lot of "anime" weapons and bosses, that flip, jump around and throw particle effects everywhere while epic music is blaring.



Then, there are the missed opportunities. First, ignoring Dark Souls 2 makes it feel like a spin-off. **Dks1 is central to Dks3's story, but Dks2 has no impact whatsoever and is barely referenced in comparison**. Instead, the game seems to worship Dks1 as often as possible. 


**For example, lots of bosses are related to the first game in a way or another:**

- the Crystal Sages and Logan


- the Abyss Watchers and Artorias


- Aldrick and Gwyndolin (though that one is pretty cool)


- the Nameless King



- the Soul of Cinder


- Oceiros and Seath



But none are related to anything from Dks2. The only returning enemy from that game ends up being the [Poison Horn Beetle](http://darksouls2.wikidot.com/poison-horn-beetle) and feral mimics, while Dark Souls 1 at least gets Black Knights and Silver Knights with enhanced movesets.


Another thing is how **the game has a geographically logical world**, which is shows you as soon as you leave the High Wall, but **afterwards is mostly linear anyway**. That kind of takes away from the whole point of that idea, and even Miyazaki acknowledged that he wish there were more connections between levels.




Then of course **there's the PvP**, which combines the most balanced invasions system of the series (1 & 2 favored the invader a lot) with gameplay mechanics that are basically a huge downgrade from 1 and 2 (the game is too fast and so is the recovery after an animation, rolls are super powerful and can be spammed, healing is almost instant and mistakes are hard to punish unless you use specific setups).




Overall, it's an incredible game, but I just wasn't expecting it to be the way it is. I still enjoy 1 and 2 way more. I know I sound super nitpicky, and I apologize for it. I just expected the game to be different than it is. Sorry if I sound salty.

Below are the only settings I have enabled in dxvk.conf. The others are commented out (with the #).


**My dxvk.conf tweaks are as follow:**

- dxgi.maxDeviceMemory = 15874 
- dxgi.maxSharedMemory = 15874



This is the **max VRAM amount you want the game to use**. I've set it to the amount that [Boris' vram tool](http://enbdev.com/download_vramsizetest.htm) indicates. Seems like VideoMemorySizeMb in enblocal.ini has no effect if you use dxvk.


- d3d9.presentInterval = 1


Enables **vsync through dxvk**. It's very smooth for me. I have set EnableVSync=false in enblocal.ini and iPresentInterval=0 in skyrim.ini.


- d3d9.samplerAnisotropy  = 16


Sets **anisotropic filtering** (texture filtering) to 16 times. I've set ForceAnisotropicFiltering=false in my enblocal.ini.


- d3d9.evictManagedOnUnlock = True


I have set ReduceSystemMemoryUsage=false in my enblocal.ini (which disables enboost I believe). I have had no out of memory crashes even though I have a rather heavy load order, so I suppose dxvk's memory management does the trick. I also use {Crash Fixes} with its OS allocators option turned on.
